content.title:
Abu Dhabi Talks Resume.
Europe Wants a Seat.
Oil Drops Below $90.
content.subject: Abu Dhabi Talks Resume. Europe Wants a Seat. Oil Drops Below $90.
content.preview_text: Ukraine talks restart, Europe pushes back and oil slides, plus the rest of the world in six minutes.
content.description: Russia and Ukraine meet in Abu Dhabi, Europe presses for a role at the G7 and COP31 settles a contested agenda.
content.contents_extra: Why oil fell below $90, global updates, trivia and your poll

stories.title: Russia and Ukraine Return to the Table in Abu Dhabi
paragraphs: Russian and Ukrainian officials met in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday for their first talks brokered by Washington since February. Reuters, via Al Monitor, reports that U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said recent contacts had narrowed the gaps. Ukraine’s Rustem Umerov said Kyiv was focused on security guarantees and a lasting peace.

Territory remains the hardest question. The BBC reports that Moscow wants Ukraine to give up the parts of Donetsk it still holds. Kyiv wants to freeze the contact line instead. A U.S. official claimed both sides had shown some private flexibility. A senior Ukrainian official strongly denied that Kyiv would consider such concessions.

stories.title: Europe Tells Washington It Belongs in Any Ukraine Deal
paragraphs: European foreign ministers used a G7 meeting in Paris to press Secretary of State Marco Rubio for a role in peace talks. Al Jazeera reports that German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said Europe belongs at this table. The two day meeting overlaps with the Abu Dhabi talks.

The friction centers on a U.S. idea for a new security architecture between Russia and Europe. The Guardian reports that EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said such an architecture already exists, and that Russia is not respecting it. Ministers from Saudi Arabia, Egypt, South Korea and Brazil are also attending, with Iran expected on Tuesday’s agenda.

photo.alt: Eiffel Tower over the Seine, 2025 file photo

stories.title: COP31 Agrees an Agenda but Leaves Adaptation Money Unresolved
paragraphs: Negotiators in Antalya adopted the COP31 agenda after late night talks. Down To Earth reports that it includes a standalone climate finance work programme, a key demand of developing countries including India. The European Union objected, arguing that the COP30 decision had not created a separate agenda item.

Other demands were left out. Proposals for separate items on tripling adaptation finance and climate related trade measures were dropped, according to the same report. India Today reports that adaptation finance and the 1.5°C limit remained unresolved as Turkey and Australia took over the joint presidency.

photo.alt: Wind turbines over farmland, 2025 file photo

deep_dive.title: Oil Slides Below $90 as Trump Signals the Iran War Is Winding Down
paragraphs: What happened. President Donald Trump said on Monday that Iran was “militarily” effectively over. Al Jazeera reports that he spoke after meeting Qatar’s prime minister at the White House. Trump said the conflict could end “fairly soon.” He added that the United States remained “locked and loaded” if circumstances changed.

The market reaction. The Guardian reports that Brent crude fell nearly 3% to $89.66 on Tuesday morning, its lowest level since August 31. CNBC reports that Brent dropped below $90 for the first time since August. Reuters, via Business Standard, reports that South Korea’s KOSPI rose more than 5% in early trading.

What is not changing. The pause does not lift pressure on Tehran. Reuters, via CNA, reports that Trump plans to keep up a naval blockade for now. The National reports that Trump said Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Bahrain and Kuwait favour maintaining it. The same arrangement includes Task Force Iron Gate, which Al Jazeera says aims to cut Iran’s land and Caspian trade.

The open question. Iran disputes the talk of diplomacy. Security council secretary Mohsen Rezaei accused Washington of manufacturing news about imaginary talks. President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran was open to negotiations but would not be coerced. An analyst quoted by The Guardian said the Federal Reserve still needs evidence of broader disinflation.

trivia.question: Who became the first science fiction author to win the Booker Prize?
trivia.explanation: M John Harrison won for The End of Everything. The Guardian reports he is also the oldest winner, at 81.

poll.question: Should European governments have a seat at Ukraine peace talks?

World view: Gaza’s first winter storm floods about 70,000 tents, Al Jazeera reports, citing Gaza’s Government Media Office, at least five deaths.
Japan grants the Philippines coastal radar and drones, Euronews reports the grant is worth 4.3 billion yen.
North Korea rejects a U.N. call for dialogue, Yonhap reports Kim Yo Jong called Antonio Guterres “prejudiced and irresponsible”.
Need to know: Sudan’s army chief meets Congo’s intelligence director, TRT Afrika reports the Khartoum talks focused on security cooperation.
Seoul subway workers threaten a November 25 strike, Yonhap reports the largest Seoul Metro union wants wage increases and more hiring.
The Marshall Islands president will visit Japan, Kyodo reports Hilda Heine will meet Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.
Money & markets: Japan’s household spending falls 6.8% in September, Kyodo reports the 10th straight monthly decline, blamed on bad weather.
Asian shares climb as oil eases, Reuters, via Business Standard, reports Japan’s Nikkei gained about 3% early.
Airline shares rise on fuel cost hopes, The Guardian reports gains for Lufthansa and Air France KLM.
Future frontiers: A cell biology puzzle from 1986 is solved, University of Liverpool researchers report that a talin region binds other talin molecules.
Earth’s core carbon may come from the outer solar system, Yale reports a study of Hawaiian melt inclusions.
Scientists report possible traces of dinosaur blood, NPR reports on a 115 million year old bone examined in Australia.
The score: Barcelona wins 2 to 1 at Atletico Madrid, Golazo lists the La Liga result in its November 9 recap.
Benfica edges Estrela 3 to 2, Golazo lists the Primeira Liga result in the same recap.
Manchester United weighs Michael Carrick’s future, The Guardian reports executives may recommend his sacking.
Life & culture: M John Harrison wins the Booker Prize, The Guardian says he is the first science fiction author to win it.
The new Booker winner is also the oldest, The Guardian reports Harrison won at 81 for The End of Everything.
A filmmaker turns his cancer treatment into a documentary, The Guardian reviews David Wilkinson’s film 1 in 2.

qa_notes.status: LOCAL_DRAFT_ONLY; parent review and combined validator required
uncertainties: Kushner says gaps narrowed; a senior Ukrainian official denies territorial concessions. No deal is claimed.
Trump says Iran war is effectively over; Iranian officials dismiss talk of talks. Blockade continues.
Brent levels differ by timestamp: $89.66 (Guardian), $90.14 at 5:33 ET (CNBC), $91.56 earlier (Business Standard). Copy uses Guardian figure and CNBC below $90 framing.
Al Monitor, Business Standard and CNA items are Reuters syndications and are attributed as such.
Gaza flood toll is from Gaza Government Media Office via Al Jazeera.
Photos are contextual file images, not event photos.
